IN 'B' GROUP, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE E.S. INDIRESH  ORAL ORDER

In this writ petition, the petitioner is assailing Preliminary Notification dated 19th August, 2003 (Annexure-B) issued by the respondent No.2 in respect of the land bearing Survey No.33/2C measuring 2222 Sq. Mtrs. of Kengal Kempohalli Village, Sompura Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk belonging to the petitioner; and award dated 31st July, 2019 (Annexure-G) passed by the respondent No.2 in respect of land bearing Survey No.33/2C measuring 514 Sq. Mtr. of Kengal Kempohalli Village, Sompura Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk; inter alia sought for direction to the respondents to pay compensation in respect of land bearing Survey No.33/2C measuring of 514 Sq.
Mtr. of Kengal Kempohalli Village, Sompura Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk.

2. The relevant facts of adjudication of this writ petition are that the respondent No.2 has issued Notification under Section 3A(1) of National Highways Act, 1956 (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'N.H. Act') and sought to acquire various properties including the land belonging to the petitioner NC: 2024:KHC:50786 WP NO.17566 OF 2022 for the purpose four laning of National Highway No.4 on the land stretch from KM-30 to KM-75 (Nelamangala to Tumkur section) in the State of Karnataka.
Thereafter, the respondent Authorities have issued notice regarding acquisition as per Annexure-C.

The respondent No.2 had passed award dated 10th October, 2003 (Annexure-D),
determining the compensation to be payable to the land loosers including the petitioner, however,
no compensation has been paid till date and therefore, the petitioner has sought for quashing the notification in respect of the subject land.

It is also stated in the petition that, the respondent-Authorities have issued a Notification dated 13th December, 2016 (Annexure-F1) and 12th December, 2017 (Annexures 'F2') and award came to be passed on 31st July, 2019 (Annexure-G), however, the respondent-Authorities have awarded compensation only insofar as the building is concerned and not assessed compensation to the land.
Hence, this writ petition.

3. Heard Sri. Keshava Murthy B., learned counsel appearing for the petitioner; Sri. Krishna Rao K.N., learned Central Government Counsel appearing for the respondent NC: 2024:KHC:50786 WP NO.17566 OF 2022 No.1; Sri. Likith, learned counsel on behalf of Sri. Sagaar Ladda, appearing for respondents 2 to 5.
4.

Sri. Keshava Murthy B., learned counsel appearing for the petitioner contended that, though the Preliminary Notification has been issued on 26th February, 2003 and award came to be passed on 10th October, 2003 (Annexure-D), however, no compensation has been deposited in the Civil Court.

He further contended that, in respect of the land bearing Survey No.33/2C measuring 514 Sq. Mtr.,
the respondent-Authorities have passed award on 31st July, 2019 (Annexure-G), assessing the compensation insofar as the building is concerned and have not assessed the award in respect of land belonging to the petitioner is concerned.
Accordingly, he sought for interference of this Court.

5. Per contra, Sri. Likith, learned appearing for the respondents 2 to 5 submitted that, in view of the dispute with regard to title of the parties is concerned, amount has not been deposited and Smt Jayamma vs Union Of India on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71464414/

sentences.text: 3 accordingly, sought to justify the action of the respondent-National Highway Authority of India.
Sri. Krishna Rao K.N., learned Central Government Counsel appearing for the respondent No.1 argued on similar lines.

7. In the light of submission made by learned counsel appearing for the parties, it is not in dispute that the Preliminary Notification was issued on 26th February, 2003 and Final Notification was issued on 19th August, 2003 (Annexure- B) to acquire the land for the purpose of construction of National Highway as stated above.
The land bearing Survey No.33/2C measuring 2222 Sq. Mtr. was sought to be acquired and award came to be passed on 10th October, 2003 (Annexure-D).

Taking into consideration the fact that the possession of land has been taken and the construction of National Highway is already laid and land being utilized for public purpose, I am of the view that,
quashing of the impugned notification at this stage would not arise, however, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, respondents 2 to 5 are directed to deposit the NC: 2024:KHC:50786 WP NO.17566 OF 2022 compensation amount in the competent Civil Court within two months from the date of receipt of this order.

8. Insofar as land bearing Survey No.33/2C measuring 514 Sq. Mtr. is concerned, the Preliminary Notification came to be issued on 13th December, 2016 (Annexure-F1) followed by Final Notification on 12th December, 2017 (Annexure-F2) and award came to be passed on 31st July, 2019 (Annexure-G).

Perusal of the proceedings of Award dated 31st July, 2019 by the respondent No.2-Special Land Acquisition Officer, National Highway Authority of India would indicate that the assessment of compensation was made only for building and compensation has not been determined for the land belonging to the petitioner.
In that view of the matter, I find force in the submission made by learned counsel appearing for the petitioner to set-aside the award dated 31st July, 2019 (Annexure-G).

Accordingly, award dated 31st July 2019 (Annexure-G) is set-aside insofar as the land belonging to the petitioner is concerned and direction is issued to the respondent No.2 to pass award in respect of the land in question including any building existing in the land, within an outer limit of two months from the date of receipt of this order.

It is also pertinent to mention here that, while determining the compensation, respondent No.2-Special Land Acquisition Officer shall conduct joint Survey at the instance of the petitioner to determine the compensation.
With these observations, writ petition stands disposed of.
